author: Gabriel Jeanson, David-Alexandre Duclos, William Larriv\'ee-Hardy, No\'e Cochet, Mat\v{e}j Boxan, Anthony Desch\^enes, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau, Philippe Gigu\`ere

title: A Benchmark for Strategic Auditee Gaming Under Continuous Compliance Monitoring
content:
arXiv:2605.06340v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Continuous post-deployment compliance audits, mandated by emerging regulations such as the EU AI Act and Digital Services Act, create a class of strategic gaming distinct from the one-shot input/output gaming studied in prior work. Regulated systems can delay outcome reporting, drift their reports within plausible noise envelopes, exploit longitudinal sample attrition, and cherry-pick among ambiguous metric definitions. We formalize continuous auditing as a $T$-round Stackelberg game between an auditor that commits to a temporal policy and an adaptive auditee, and identify a structural feature of any noise-aware static-auditor design: a cover regime in which coverage gaps and granularity gaps cannot be closed simultaneously. We make this formal as Observation 1 and show that two minimal extension policies, each derived from the observation, close the regime along orthogonal axes: a sample-size-aware static rule (Periodic-with-floor) closes the granularity-failure case, while a history-conditioned suspicion-escalation policy closes the coverage-failure case for the naive Drift strategy -- and neither closes both, exactly as the observation predicts; an audit-aware OffAuditDrift strategy that exploits Stackelberg commitment defeats both. To support empirical study we contribute a non-additive harm decomposition (welfare loss $W$, coverage loss $C$) that exposes how attrition shifts harm from the regulator-accountable surface to a regulator-invisible one; an initial library of five auditee strategies (Delay, Drift, Cherry-pick, Attrition, OffAuditDrift) and five auditor policies, calibrated to summary statistics from published audits of the DSA Transparency Database; and a reproducible simulator with a small, extensible Python interface.
author: Florian A. D. Burnat, Brittany I. Davidson

title: Quotient Semivalues for False-Name-Resistant Data Attribution
content:
arXiv:2605.07663v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Data valuation methods allocate payments and audit training data's contribution to machine-learning pipelines; however, they often assume passive contributors. In reality, contributors can split datasets across pseudonymous identities, duplicate high-value examples, create near-duplicates, or launder synthetic variants to inflate their share. We formalize this as false-name manipulation in ML data attribution. Our main construction is the quotient semivalue mechanism: compute Shapley-, Banzhaf-, or Beta-style values over evidence-backed attribution clusters instead of raw identities, using a canonical-representative operator to absorb within-cluster duplication. We prove an impossibility: on a fixed monotone data-value game, exact Shapley-fair attribution over reported identities is incompatible with unrestricted false-name-proofness, even on binary-valued instances, and characterize the split-gain of a general semivalue on a unanimity counter-example. The mechanism is exactly false-name-proof under two structural conditions: false-name-neutral within-cluster allocation and quotient-stable manipulations. Under imperfect provenance, when these conditions hold approximately, manipulation gain and fairness loss are bounded by three measurable quantities: escaped-cluster mass, value-estimation error, and clustering distance. We instantiate the mechanisms in DataMarket-Gym, a benchmark for attribution under strategic provider attacks. On synthetic classification tasks, quotient semivalues with example-level evidence reduce manipulation gain on duplicate and near-duplicate Sybil attacks from $1.74$ under baseline Shapley to $0.96$, near the honest level. The cosine-threshold and (false-merge, false-split) rate sweeps trace the corresponding fairness--Sybil frontier.
author: Florian A. D. Burnat, Brittany I. Davidson

title: Differentially Private Auditing Under Strategic Response
content:
arXiv:2605.07674v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Regulatory audits of AI systems increasingly rely on differential privacy (DP) to protect training data and model internals. We study audit design when the audited developer can strategically respond to the privacy-constrained audit interface. We formalize privacy-constrained auditing as a bilevel Stackelberg game, in which an auditor commits to a query policy and DP budget allocation across harm dimensions, and a strategic developer reallocates mitigation efforts in response. We introduce the welfare-weighted under-detection gap $B_w$, the welfare-weighted true residual harm the audit fails to detect at the developer's strategic best response, and prove that naive DP auditing (uniform or harm-proportional allocation) induces a strictly larger $B_w$ than any non-strategic mitigation baseline whenever effective detectability is heterogeneous, the welfare weights are not comonotone with detectability, and the developer's optimum is interior. We characterize the optimal auditor allocation as a four-factor balance of welfare weight, audit miss-probability, detectability elasticity, and mitigation-cost curvature, and provide a single-level reformulation of the bilevel problem via the developer's KKT system. We propose Strategic Private Audit Design (SPAD), a projected-gradient algorithm with hypergradients computed through the developer's best response.
author: Florian A. D. Burnat

title: AI4BayesCode: From Natural Language Descriptions to Validated Modular Stateful Bayesian Samplers
content:
arXiv:2605.18476v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Coding and computation remain major bottlenecks in Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) workflows, especially as modern sampling algorithms have become increasingly complex and existing probabilistic programming systems remain limited in model support, extensibility, and composability. We introduce \textbf{AI4BayesCode}, an extensible LLM-driven system that translates natural-language Bayesian model descriptions into runnable, validated MCMC samplers. To improve reliability, AI4BayesCode adopts a modular design that decomposes models into modular sampling blocks and maps each block to a built-in sampling component, reducing the need to implement complex sampling algorithms from scratch. Reliability is further improved through pre-generation validation of model specifications and post-generation validation of generated sampler code. AI4BayesCode also introduces a novel recursively stateful coding paradigm for MCMC, allowing modular sampling components, potentially developed by different contributors, to be composed coherently within larger MCMC procedures. We develop a benchmark suite to evaluate AI4BayesCode for sampler-generation. Experiments show that AI4BayesCode can implement a wide range of Bayesian models from natural-language descriptions alone. As an open-ended system, its capability can continue to expand with improvements in the underlying AI agent and the addition of new built-in blocks. The software is available at https://ai4bayescode.com/.
author: Jungang Zou, Alex Ziyu Jiang, Qixuan Chen

title: ChangeDINO: Bi-Level Feature Entanglement Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection With Vision–Language Prior
content: The performance of most existing remote sensing change detection (RSCD) methods is often constrained by limited semantic understanding and a heavy dependence on large volumes of training data. To address these limitations, we propose ChangeDINO, a novel change detection paradigm that effectively integrates both semantic knowledge and positional information from Grounding DINO, a representative open-vocabulary detector. To fully leverage Grounding DINO’s semantic guidance and object localization capabilities, we introduce a bi-level feature entanglement strategy, incorporating two key components: the semantically guided fusion module (SGFM) and the position-aware enhancement module (PEM). The SGFM adaptively exploits the spatially heterogeneous activation patterns of features from the open-vocabulary detector as semantic guidance signals, selectively amplifying the contribution of high-activation object regions while suppressing uninformative background responses. The PEM, in turn, exploits positional embeddings from cross-modal queries and applies feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) for pixel-level calibration, thereby enhancing spatial precision and refining boundary localization of changed regions. Together, these mechanisms enable ChangeDINO to transfer fine-grained semantics and precise positional cues from large-scale vision–language pretraining into the RSCD task, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on standard benchmarks—LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD—as well as on our newly proposed AUUCDD, with  $F1$ -scores of 92.89%, 95.79%, 83.87%, and 90.17%, respectively. Furthermore, experiments under data-scarce conditions demonstrate that ChangeDINO maintains superior performance by leveraging Grounding DINO’s rich pretrained representations, thereby reducing dependence on task-specific annotations and providing a practical solution for data-limited scenarios. The code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/G124556/ChangeDINO
author: Yupeng Gao, Tianyu Li, Guoqing Wang, Peng Wang, Jiayi Ma, Yang Yang

title: Coarse-to-Fine Nonrigid Registration for Side-Scan Sonar Mosaicking
content: Side-scan sonar (SSS) mosaicking plays a crucial role in large-scale seabed mapping but is challenged by complex nonlinear, spatially varying distortions due to diverse sonar acquisition conditions. Existing rigid or affine registration methods fail to model such complex deformations, whereas traditional nonrigid techniques tend to overfit and lack robustness in sparse-texture sonar data. To address these challenges, we propose a coarse-to-fine hierarchical nonrigid registration framework tailored for large-scale SSS images. Our method begins with a global thin plate spline (TPS) initialization from sparse correspondences, followed by superpixel-guided segmentation that partitions the image into structurally consistent patches preserving terrain integrity. Each patch is then refined by a pretrained SynthMorph network in an unsupervised manner, enabling dense and flexible alignment without task-specific training. Finally, a fusion strategy integrates both global and local deformations into a smooth, unified deformation field. Extensive quantitative and visual evaluations demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art rigid, classical nonrigid, and learning-based methods in accuracy, structural consistency, and deformation smoothness on the challenging sonar dataset.
author: Can Lei, Nuno Gracias, Rafael Garcia, Hayat Rajani, Huigang Wang

title: Hierarchical Feature Integration Network for Bi-Temporal Remote Sensing Change Detection Under Complex Environmental Conditions
content: Change detection in high-resolution remote sensing images is affected by various complex factors. Our principal component analysis (PCA) analysis reveals distinct feature clustering in normal environments, contrasting with overlapping, blurred-boundary distributions in complex environments. This blurring arises from seasonal variations, weather conditions, loss of fine-grained textural information, and the inherent difficulty of detecting changed areas. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical feature integration network inspired by the human visual system (HVS), integrating model-driven and data-driven approaches by mimicking the HVS’s selective and nonselective pathways. Specifically, curvature-sensitive and fractional-order modules, simulating the nonselective pathway’s capacity for rapid geometric and textural processing, enhance edges via curvature flow equations and detect fine-grained textural variations using fractional-order parameters. Then, we design a cognitive attention-based data-driven module to simulate the selective pathway of HVS, adjusting feature weights for complex environment adaptation. Finally, a visual area V2-inspired knowledge detection head (KDH) integrates the fast, low-level features from the nonselective pathway and the slow, high-level features from the selective pathway, using an integrated loss function that balances interpretability and learning capacity, achieving  $F1$ -scores of 93.33%, 94.17%, 90.15%, and 90.61% on LEVIR, DSIFN, CDD, and SYS datasets, respectively, outperforming nine competing methods with improvements up to +11.69% in F1, while maintaining a lightweight architecture of 11.45-M parameters and 26.72-G FLOPs, providing a robust solution for high-resolution remote sensing image change detection (HRRS-CD) in complex environments. Codes are available at our https://github.com/Zzzz12349/HVS-CHANGE
author: Zhi Li, Siying Cao, Shun Lv, Shaobing Gao, Zhenming Peng, Yiguang Liu

title: Model Study of Microwave Signatures of Bistatic Scattering From a Rice Canopy
content: In this article, we present a microwave bistatic scattering model of rice canopy based on radiative transfer theory. Then, the bistatic scattering response of a rice canopy across the entire growth stage is analyzed, accounting for canopy components and their interactions with radar parameters, such as polarization, incident angle, and frequency. Comparison between model predictions and available field measurements was conducted for the special case of monostatic backscattering at L-, S-, C-, and X-bands. The results show that the model captures the general temporal trends and polarization-dependent behavior of measured backscattering coefficients across rice growth stages. Numerical simulation results indicate that the bistatic scattering coefficients are highly dependent on observation geometries and the rice plant’s growth stage. Compared to a monostatic system, the bistatic configuration leads to enhanced variation in co-polarized backscatter during early growth stages and an increased cross-polarized response during the ripening stage, resulting in larger dynamic ranges and stronger contrast between growth stages than in the monostatic case. The role of canopy structural components (stems, leaves, and panicles) in shaping bistatic scattering responses, the dependence of scattering behavior on observation geometry, and the stage-dependent transition between co-polarized and cross-polarized dominance.
author: Kun-Shan Chen, Ying Yang, Yu Liu

title: RSUS: A Novel Upsampling Layer for Semantic Segmentation Network of Remote Sensing Images
content: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing images (RSIs) often struggles with boundary blurring, structural discontinuity, and category confusion due to limitations in conventional interpolation and dynamic upsampling methods. This article proposes RSUS, a new upsampling layer designed to preserve semantic consistency and spatial structure. RSUS consists of three components: 1) global context vector aggregation (GCVA) for content-aware prediction kernels that introduce global priors into local feature reconstruction; 2) cross-scale anisotropic implicit positional encoding (CAIPE) for direction-sensitive spatial deformation and structural alignment; and 3) adaptive high-frequency structure gating (AHSG) to enhance boundary-related frequency responses. In addition, persistent homology (PH) is used as a topological analysis tool to assess connectivity and structure preservation beyond pixel-level metrics. Extensive experiments on five datasets (International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS) Vaihingen, ISPRS Potsdam, LoveDA, UAVid, and Xining) demonstrate that RSUS improves performance across mainstream segmentation networks, outperforming advanced upsampling methods. Analyses show RSUS alleviates structural misalignment, improves category consistency, and recovers fine-grained boundaries in remote sensing segmentation. The source code is available at: https://github.com/Ronin-711/RSUS
author: Yaning Liu, Ronghao Yang, Shaoda Li, Junxiang Tan, Guyue Hu, Chenghao Liu, Yunfan Luo, Zhiqiu Liang, Tian Dong

title: Induction Logging Through Casing by Detecting Lateral Waves: Reduced-Scale Experiments
content: Through-casing induction logging (TCIL) is a dream technology in the field of petroleum logging. However, due to the high conductivity of steel casing, sinusoidal electromagnetic field is severely shielded by the casing, and therefore, the development of TCIL tool is very difficult. Recently, a lateral-wave TCIL strategy has been proposed with enhanced formation sensitivity and reduced casing imprint. The main difficulty is that the lateral wave is very weak. This article reports the experimental results by using reduced-scale stainless steel casings to test the principle of lateral-wave TCIL strategy. Employing brine tanks as an analog for the subsurface formation, the phase difference is detected between the induced voltages in two receiver coils located at two different positions in the remote lateral-wave dominant region. With increased brine salinity, the phase difference increases notably, demonstrating the sensitivity for detecting the conductivity of the brine. More importantly, at increased working frequency, the phase difference in the presence of the casing trends that in the absence of the casing, providing evidence for the validity of the principle of lateral-wave TCIL.
author: Fazhong Shen, Zirun Yao, Qiangli Xi

title: TP-Mamba: Topological Semantic Convergence and Prototype Recalibration for HSI Classification
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification (CLS) entails two fundamental challenges: local semantic discontinuity caused by multiclass mixing and global semantic drift exacerbated by long-range propagation in state-space models. To address these issues, we propose TP-Mamba, a novel framework that jointly restores local topological continuity and recalibrates global semantic drift. To repair local semantic discontinuity, we propose a topological semantic convergence module (TSCM) to fill interior holes and reconnect boundary-adjacent fragments along the channel dimension. To recalibrate global semantic drift, we design a text-guided prototype retrieval module (TPRM) that distills class-specific intrinsic features from drifted representations via class-wise text prompts and aggregates them into a compact semantic prototype for global recalibration. To mitigate the over-reliance on textual priors, we propose a prototype spatial modulation-drop (PSM-Drop) block that selectively activates the prototype branch via a Bernoulli dropout strategy while adaptively injecting the prototype into appropriate spatial positions through channel-aware gating. Experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that TP-Mamba achieves superior performance over recent state-of-the-art HSIC methods. Ablation and visualization results further verify the effectiveness of each component. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/shiqiCraig/TP-Mamba
author: Junliang Chen, Xinpeng Zhang, Fan Shi, Cheng Jiang, Xu Cheng, Shengyong Chen

title: A Stagewise Spectral-Structural Coordinated Reconstruction Network for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
content: Hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HMIF) aims to reconstruct high-resolution hyperspectral images (HR-HSIs) by integrating the rich spectral information of low-resolution hyperspectral images (LR-HSIs) with the fine spatial details of high-resolution multispectral images (HR-MSIs). In most existing methods, emphasis is still placed primarily on representation alignment, frequency enhancement, or progressive refinement, whereas the role of structural information throughout hyperspectral reconstruction has not been systematically distinguished with respect to its intervention timing, cross-modal transferability, and back-projection mechanism into the physical spectral-band domain. In particular, when cross-modal responses are inconsistent, spectral shifts and spurious textures may readily be induced by unconstrained or premature structural injection. To address this issue, a stagewise spectral-structural coordination network, termed SSCNet, is proposed. HMIF is reformulated as a constrained structural participation problem, and coordination between spectral preservation and spatial compensation is achieved through stagewise structural modulation. Specifically, SSCNet first constructs a hyperspectral-image-dominated (HSI-dominated) latent spectral basis; it then performs cross-modal screening of multispectral image (MSI) high-frequency structures under spectral guidance; finally, the screened structural information is progressively converted into reconstruction gains for HR-hyperspectral images (HSIs) through stagewise fusion back-projection. Experimental results on four datasets under  $4\times $ ,  $8\times $ , and  $16\times $  degradation settings demonstrate that SSCNet achieves competitive performance across eight evaluation metrics, while exhibiting lower reconstruction error and reduced computational complexity. The code will be made available at https://github.com/LRuiRui517/SSCNetwork
author: Ruiping Liu, Jie Li, Pan Wang, Chunyu Zhu

title: ArtFusion: An Arbitrary-Reference Spatiotemporal Fusion Model for Seamless Remote Sensing Image Reconstruction
content: Spatiotemporal fusion (STF) represents a vital solution for continuous high-resolution Earth observation. Despite the increasing abundance of historical satellite archives, most existing STF methods are constrained by a limited number of auxiliary reference images (typically one or two), leading to underutilized multitemporal information and reduced reconstruction reliability, particularly when References are compromised by cloud contamination or abrupt land-surface variations. To address these limitations, this study proposes an arbitrary-reference STF (ArtFusion) model. The architecture incorporates an efficient contrast-aware hybrid block (ECHB) for deep feature extraction, an explicit temporal information encoder (ETIE) to utilize acquisition metadata, and a multihead cross-reference attention fusion (MCAF) module designed to facilitate the integration of an arbitrary number of reference images. A comprehensive evaluation across 24 experimental cases in three representative study regions demonstrates that ArtFusion consistently outperforms four state-of-the-art (SOTA) benchmarks [multilevel feature fusion with generative adversarial network (MLFF-GAN), C-ROBOT, RealFusion, and frequency-selected differential fusion transformer (FSDFormer)]. Compared with the best-performing baseline among the four competing methods, ArtFusion achieves average improvements of 6.8% in spectral accuracy [root-mean-square error (RMSE)] and 15.3% in spatial accuracy [improved edge difference metric (iEDGE)]. Notably, high reliability is maintained across four challenging scenarios: rapid phenological changes, drastic morphological variations, highly heterogeneous landscapes, and frequent cloud contamination, while also demonstrating strong cross-regional transferability. Despite its superior performance, ArtFusion has an extremely compact structure with 0.19 million trainable parameters, only 2.2% of MLFF-GAN’s parameters. This work demonstrates the potential of leveraging multiple reference images to push the boundaries of STF accuracy, rather than merely increasing model complexity. This flexible multireference fusion scheme provides a promising pathway for robust, large-scale Earth observation in cloudy and dynamically changing landscapes. The source code is available at: https://github.com/Andy-cumt/ArtFusion-STF
author: Dizhou Guo, Qianqian Jia, Xuan Wang, Yinze Lian, Zhenhong Li

title: Closed-Loop Remote Sensing Image Change Detection via Active Difference-Prior Guidance
content: Deep learning-based methods have achieved remarkable progress in urban change detection (CD) from high-resolution remote sensing (RS) images. However, most existing methods treat different information merely as a static output, without allowing the statistical and semantic priors embedded in it to continuously guide subsequent inference. As a result, they remain limited in both pseudo-change suppression and multiscale change representation. To address these issues, this article proposes a difference-prior-guided network (DPGNet). First, a statistical prior-guided rectification module (SPRM) is developed to derive priors from the statistical characteristics of bitemporal features, which are then used to jointly compensate for imaging-style discrepancies, thereby yielding more discriminative difference representations from the outset. Second, a difference retrospective probe (DRP) is designed to treat preliminary difference features as hypothesized priors and revisit the original spatiotemporal context to verify whether the detected changes are genuine, thereby further refining change semantics. Finally, a semantic prior-guided aggregation module (SPGA) exploits big difference features as global semantic priors to guide shallow detail features toward semantic alignment, thus preserving the structural integrity of large-scale targets while enhancing sensitivity to subtle changes. On the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD datasets, DPGNet achieves  $F1$ -scores of 92.35%, 94.49%, and 84.16%, respectively, outperforming existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods and validating its effectiveness for urban CD from high-resolution RS images. Meanwhile, DPGNet contains only 7.75-M parameters and 8.66-G floating-point operations (FLOPs), showing a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency. In addition, DPGNet still has room for improvement in detecting change regions with ambiguous boundaries and extremely small and spatially scattered change targets. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/AspirinRS/DPGNet
author: Jingyu Yang, Jiayang Li, Chengqi Bao, Jiyuan Li, Jianwu Dang, Jiaxin Li

title: A Lightweight Multiscale Fusion Framework for Traffic Vehicle Detection From Satellite Remote Sensing, UAV, and CCTV Imagery
content: Vehicle detection from heterogeneous traffic imagery is essential for large-scale traffic monitoring. However, satellite remote sensing, uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV), and closed-circuit television (CCTV) images differ substantially in spatial resolution, viewing geometry, illumination conditions, and vehicle scale, making unified cross-source detection challenging, especially for small targets and unseen source-domain distributions. To address these issues, this study proposes a lightweight source-conditioned multiscale detection framework for vehicle detection from independent satellite, UAV, and CCTV image domains. The framework is centered on a source-aware multiscale awareness fusion module (SA-MS-AFM), which performs source-expert reweighting from a single input image and supports masked-expert training for incomplete expert availability. SwiftFormer with efficient additive attention (EAA) is adopted for efficient local–global representation, while Shiftwise convolution enhances local structural cues with low overhead. Content-aware reassembly of features (CARAFEs) is introduced in the neck to reduce spatial-detail loss during top-down feature reconstruction, and a four-scale prediction head is designed to accommodate large vehicle-scale variations. Experiments on a pooled cross-source dataset of 6805 images show that the proposed model achieves an  $F_{1}$ -score of 0.885, mAP@0.5 of 0.886, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.513 while maintaining 41.53 frames per second (FPS) on the tested RTX 4090 GPU. Ablation, expert-masking, three-scale/four-scale tradeoff, and zero-shot external generalization tests further demonstrate the effectiveness and transferability of the proposed framework under heterogeneous traffic imaging conditions.
author: Zhen Liu, Mei-Po Kwan, Weiwei Jiang, Yang Liu, Bingyan Cui

title: CGFT: Cross-Guided Fusion Transformer for Multimodal Multiview Scene Recognition
content: Multimodal learning aims to learn comprehensive representations by integrating complementary information from different perspectives. However, multimodal images acquired from heterogeneous sensor systems frequently exhibit substantial representation gaps, making multimodal fusion a challenging task. Existing methods often struggle to model semantic correspondences across different modalities, resulting in feature misalignment that hinders effective multimodal representation learning. To address this issue, we propose a cross-guided fusion transformer (CGFT) for multimodal multiview remote sensing scene recognition. CGFT improves feature alignment through a progressive coarse-to-fine refinement of cross-modal correspondences. Specifically, we first bridge the representation discrepancy by comparing features across modalities with an instance-level contrastive learning loss. Then, we propose a fine-grained alignment module with a sophisticated cross-attention mechanism that explicitly refines semantic correspondences by aligning relevant tokens with cross-modal query-focused guidance. Furthermore, we adopt a multimodal feature fusion scheme with modality-wise weighting to enhance the complementary integration of multimodal features. This strategy effectively promotes the fine-grained cross-modal alignment while suppressing the noisy correspondence problem, thereby leading to enhanced performance in complex real-world scenarios. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
author: Kun Li, Lizhuo Liu, Zhenpeng Feng, Zhunga Liu

title: Deep Imbalanced Multitarget Regression: 3-D Point Cloud Voxel Content Estimation in Simulated Forests
content: Voxelization is an effective approach to reduce the computational cost of processing light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data; yet, it results in a loss of fine-scale structural information. This study explores whether low-level voxel content information, specifically target occupancy percentage within a voxel, can be inferred from high-level voxelized LiDAR point cloud data collected from Digital Imaging and Remote Sensing Image Generation (DIRSIG) software. In our study, the targets include bark, leaf, soil, and miscellaneous materials. We propose a multitarget regression approach in the context of imbalanced learning using kernel point convolutions (KPConvs). Our research leverages cost-sensitive learning to address class imbalance called density-based relevance (DBR). We employ weighted mean squared error (WMSE), focal regression (FocalR), and regularization to improve the optimization of KPConv. This study performs a sensitivity analysis on the voxel size (0.25–2 m) to evaluate the effect of various grid representations in capturing the nuances of the forest. This sensitivity analysis reveals that larger voxel sizes (e.g., 2 m) result in lower errors due to reduced variability, while smaller voxel sizes (e.g., 0.25 or 0.5 m) exhibit higher errors, particularly within the canopy, where variability is greatest. For bark and leaf targets, error values at smaller voxel size datasets (0.25 and 0.5 m) were significantly higher than those in larger voxel size datasets (2 m), highlighting the difficulty in accurately estimating within-canopy voxel content at fine resolutions. This suggests that the choice of voxel size is application-dependent. Our work fills the gap in deep imbalance learning models for multitarget regression and simulated datasets for 3-D LiDAR point clouds of forests.
author: Amirhossein Hassanzadeh, Bartosz Krawczyk, Michael Saunders, Robert Wible, Keith Krause, Dimah Dera, Jan van Aardt

title: Multidirectional Wavefield-Decomposition Elastic Reverse-Time Migration With Dip-Guided Imaging Conditions
content: Elastic reverse-time migration (ERTM) solves the two-way elastic wave equation to image both PP and converted PS waves. In conventional ERTM, filtering can attenuate the low-frequency noise caused by near  $180~^{\circ }$ C cross correlations, but low-wavenumber and velocity-gradient artifacts still degrade the images. De-primary ERTM (Dp-ERTM) performs wavefield decomposition and forms images by cross correlating the downgoing source-side wavefield with the upgoing receiver-side wavefield. This strategy effectively suppresses low-wavenumber and velocity-gradient artifacts. However, in complex structural settings, up- and downgoing wave decomposition cannot reliably distinguish reflection energy from transmission energy. As a result, reflections from steeply dipping structures may leak into discarded components, attenuating their imaging energy. To address these limitations, we propose a dip-guided multidirectional wavefield decomposition ERTM imaging condition. A polarity-preserved outward normal dip-angle field is estimated from the structure tensor and velocity-gradient polarity. Multidirectional wavefield decomposition is implemented with Hilbert transforms along arbitrary directions. The dip-angle information constrains the directions of the wavefield components used in the imaging cross correlation, thereby preserving effective reflection energy consistent with complex structural trends. Numerical examples on the simple salt-dome, BP, and SEAM models show that the method achieves artifact suppression comparable to Dp-ERTM while better preserving the energy that illuminates dipping structures steeply.
author: Xiaoting Zhou, Xiyan Zhou, Teng Hu, Shaohuan Zu, Xiaotao Wen

title: Beyond Nighttime Lights: Multisensor Satellite Fusion for Province-Constrained District-Level GDP Disaggregation in Data-Scarce Regions
content: AAccurate subnational measures of economic activity are essential for spatial policy, particularly in developing and middle-income countries with pronounced regional inequalities. Yet official statistics are often unavailable at fine administrative scales, leaving local dynamics poorly captured. This study develops a transparent, scalable framework for province-constrained small-area GDP disaggregation in data-scarce settings, using Türkiye as a case study. Because districtlevel GDP is not officially available, the framework uses the Socio-Economic Development Index (SEDI) as a supervisory benchmark to learn relative intraprovincial socioeconomic structure. This learned structure is combined with multisource satellite and demographic indicators to allocate official provincial GDP totals to districts while preserving aggregate consistency. The framework integrates complementary indicators capturing different dimensions of production and socioeconomic activity: artificial illumination from VIIRS nighttime lights, vegetation dynamics from MODIS NDVI, structural density from Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter, and pollution from Sentinel-5P NO2, complemented by population and surface area to represent demographic scale and spatial heterogeneity. Using province-grouped cross-validation to compare models, Random Forest provided the most stable performance under spatially conservative validation. Resulting signals become province-specific allocation weights within a mass-preserving dasymetric procedure. Three findings emerge: light-only indicators are insufficient for capturing fine-scale variation, especially in heterogeneous or rural regions; integrating multiple satellite and demographic indicators improves representation of intraprovincial heterogeneity relative to single-source approaches; and the aggregate-consistent district estimates align meaningfully with external benchmarks, interpreted as convergent statistical associations rather than direct causal validation. The study offers a transferable approach for countries where official economic statistics remain spatially limited.
author: Anıl Güzel, Fırat Gündem

title: A Novel Soil Moisture Retrieval Model Using Dynamic Spatiotemporal Error Propagation for CYGNSS
content: Spaceborne global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) has emerged as an effective technique for global soil moisture retrieval. However, the accuracy of SM estimation using a single GNSS-R observable is limited by land surface heterogeneity. While incorporating auxiliary parameters can improve model performance, it often increases dependency on external data. Conventional methods relying solely on GNSS-R reflectivity also struggle to mitigate the impact of dynamic spatiotemporal errors on retrieval accuracy. This study proposes a novel SM retrieval method using dynamic spatiotemporal error propagation based on cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS) data. First, the bias variation for each quasi-global grid is derived using a traditional CYGNSS reflectivity-based SM retrieval model. The overall error trend is then fitted via a dual-branch wavelet neural network algorithm. Finally, an improved retrieval model is constructed by integrating the fitted error with CYGNSS reflectivity. Validation demonstrated that the proposed model achieved an RMSE of 0.049 cm3/cm3—a reduction of 20.97% compared with the traditional model when using soil moisture active passive (SMAP) products as reference. The correlation coefficient (R) increased from 0.876 to 0.923. More pronounced improvements were observed over farmland, where RMSE decreased by 42.11% and R increased by 37.5%. Using International Soil Moisture Network measurements as reference, the average RMSE decreased by 7.04%, R increased by 72.29%, and unbiased RMSE decreased by 7.27%. Compared with the machine learning models, the proposed method also showed superior accuracy. In addition, an independent verification was conducted with the ERA5-land SM data product, and a sensitivity analysis was performed on the error structure of SMAP to further evaluate the robustness and independence of the proposed method. These results indicate that the model enhances the accuracy of spaceborne GNSS-R-based SM monitoring without relying on auxiliary data.
author: Fade Chen, Xuetao Yuan, Lilong Liu, Liangke Huang, Fei Guo, Yuanfa Ji

title: A Downsamplable Inverse ERMA Method for Hybrid SAR-ISAR Imaging Framework of Maneuvering Ship Target
content: For radar imaging of the maneuvering ship target, the synthetic aperture radar-inverse mapping-inverse synthetic aperture radar (SAR-IM-ISAR) framework using range migration algorithm (RMA) suffers from high computational complexity in IM and ISAR processes due to the high pulse repetition frequency. In this article, the SAR-IM-ISAR framework employing an extended range migration algorithm (ERMA) is proposed. The ERMA focuses the image on the azimuth spatial frequency domain through an improved STOLT interpolation model. It benefits the data downsampling of inverse ERMA processing. We first explain the fundamental theory of traditional RMAs difficulty in achieving data downsampling. Then, the azimuth spatial position-dependent quadratic phase model is constructed through the proposed interpolation kernel, and radar image focusing in the azimuth spatial frequency domain is realized by azimuth matched filtering. Finally, inverse ERMA and ISAR processing is applied to defocused image slices of the ship target, achieving the data downsampling and refocusing imaging. In this article, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through SAR imaging and SAR-IM-ISAR processing experiments. These experiments utilize radar echoes generated based on target pose information provided by a 6-DoF motion model. The echoes were generated separately using both the traditional scattering point model and the electromagnetic simulation model.
author: Zhixin Wu, Yanbin Liu, Shuxian Dong, Yang Liu, Min Xue, Yuexin Gao, Letian Guo, Mengdao Xing

title: Iterative Least-Squares Collocation Bathymetry Inversion With Optimized Gravity Covariance
content: Bathymetry inversion using least-squares collocation (LSC) from satellite altimetry gravity data often relies on empirical covariance parameters or prior topography information, which is physically inconsistent with actual inversion conditions. This article presents an iterative LSC method for bathymetry estimation that strictly uses only observed gravity anomalies to construct the covariance model. We determine the optimal parameters A and B of the Tscherning/Rapp gravity anomaly covariance function directly from the gravity field model, rather than using empirical values. The topography covariance is derived via covariance propagation, and its conversion coefficients from gravity covariance are iteratively optimized for improved consistency and numerical stability. Compared with conventional linear regression, the proposed LSC framework further considers nonlinear terms of bathymetry. In addition to conventional shipborne check points, the residual terrain model is introduced as an independent supplementary validation to assess geophysical consistency. Experiments in the South China Sea show that the method provides physically reasonable and consistent bathymetry results with good coherence with existing models.
author: Diao Fan, Shanshan Li, Xianyong Pei, Jinkai Feng, Jinhui Zhang, Shuqiang Xue

title: A Robust Seabed Sediment Classification Method Based on Multifeature Fusion
content: Seabed sediment classification using multibeam echosounder (MBES) data, such as bathymetry, backscatter angular response (AR), and backscatter mosaic, has the advantages of being faster and less costly than the traditional seafloor grab sampling. However, the complex ocean environment leads to serious noise in the backscatter data, which affects the feature extraction and further reduces the classification accuracy. In this article, we proposed a robust seabed sediment classification method based on multifeature fusion. We used an approach to accurately extract AR features by combining the RANSAC algorithm and generic seafloor acoustic backscatter model. This approach is capable of removing outliers in backscatter strength (BS) caused by residual beam patterns. Meanwhile, object-based image analysis can extract image features from objects with larger-scales and semantic shapes to suppress the influence of high-frequency noise and small-scale outliers. It was used to reduce the effects of speckle and stripe noise in BS mosaic feature extraction. A feature set integrating AR features, backscatter mosaic features, and bathymetric features was used for sediment classification. The proposed method was applied to the MBES data from Jiaozhou Bay. After examining the classification results, it was observed that the root mean square error (RMSE) of the AR curve decreased from 2.57 to 1.64 dB. In addition, the importance score of backscatter mosaic features increased from 0.7 to 1.0.
author: Quanyin Zhang, Jianhu Zhao, Shaobo Li

title: A Plug-and-Play Data-Centric Training Framework for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Current approaches predominantly treat hyperspectral image (HSI) classification as a standard computer vision task, relying on static training paradigms that ignore HSI’s unique physical attributes—specifically, severe spectral redundancy and high spatial correlation. This oversight leads to exorbitant computational costs. To break this bottleneck, we present the progressive adaptive constrained efficient (PACE) framework. As a plug-and-play scheme, PACE introduces dynamic training optimization, seamlessly integrating with various architectures without structural modifications. Specifically, PACE consists of three synergistic modules: first, the spatial-spectral dual-constraint data augmentation module leverages spatial homogeneity and continuous spectral signatures to generate physically consistent pseudo-labeled samples, effectively addressing data scarcity. Second, the Progressive gradient descent strategy implements a dynamic curriculum that progressively refines data sampling, substantially reducing computational redundancy. Third, the input–output coupled adaptive focusing mechanism adaptively focuses optimization on reliable features, ensuring stable convergence. Extensive experiments across 11 representative HSI classification architectures on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that PACE consistently achieves overall accuracy improvements of 1.33%, 1.08%, 1.91%, and 0.92% on the Salinas, Pavia University, WHU-LongKou, and HyRANK-Loukia datasets, respectively, alongside a total training time reduction of 35.92%, 21.39%, 22.14%, and 21.13% on these datasets, respectively, offering a practical and universal solution that effectively balances efficiency and accuracy in HSI classification.
author: Xinhao Li, Hong Xie, Li Yan, Mingming Xu, Wenfei Shen, Hengtong Shen, Jiang Song, Weili Guo, Yaxuan Wei

title: Refining Estimates of Vegetation Water Storage From SMAP L-Band VOD Using GEDI Canopy Height Observations
content: Vegetation water storage (VWS), defined as the water mass contained in plant tissues per unit ground area, is a small but dynamic component of the terrestrial water cycle. VWS is commonly scaled from microwave vegetation optical depth (VOD) via a linear parameter “$b$”. While $b$-parameters are well studied for grasslands and croplands, they remain uncertain in forests, where spatially extensive reference VWS observations have been unavailable at radiometer resolutions. In this study, we address this gap by rescaling Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) ancillary VWS estimates using Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) canopy height maps, incorporating observed vegetation structure as a first-order constraint on water storage capacity. Canopy height rescaling significantly reduces saturation effects in the previously published VWS dataset and increases VWS heterogeneity across landscapes. New $b$-parameters were estimated by land cover type with VOD products from the SMAP dual channel algorithm (DCA) and multitemporal DCA (MT-DCA) and both the original and height-scaled VWS references. Updated forest $b$-parameters average 0.067, roughly half of their previously assigned values, indicating greater water storage in forests than was assumed. The resulting estimates of the global vegetation water pool proved sensitive to both the chosen $b$-parameters and the VOD algorithm, ranging from 408 to 609 km$^{3}$ across all combinations. Updated $b$-parameters attribute a larger fraction of this global pool to evergreen broadleaf forests and savanna ecosystems. These changes highlight the need for independent measurements of vegetation structure in deriving reference estimates of VWS.
author: Duncan Jurayj, Jessica V. Fayne

title: A Hybrid Visual Mamba Network With Global-Local Perception for Land Use and Land Cover Semantic Segmentation
content: Aiming to address limitations in modeling global context and local details in current remote sensing image (RSI) segmentation for land use and land cover, a hybrid visual Mamba model (HVMM) based on global sensing and local details is introduced to gain a deeper understanding of RSIs. The proposed HVMM framework combines two core components: a hybrid visual Mamba block with global and local features (HVMB) and a cross-scale attention aggregation (CSAA) module. The HVMB captures long-term dependency and aggregates multiscale features, thereby boosting the high-fidelity representations. Concurrently, the CSAA module mitigates feature distribution discrepancies across different scales, ensuring robust generalization capabilities. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including LoveDA and UAVid, conclude that HVMM achieves an OA of 77.86% and 88.02%, an mF1 of 80.05% and 80.41, and an mIoU of 63.01% and 71.13%, respectively, notably improving segmentation accuracy and supervision efficiency of land use.
author: Jie Tang, Junhong Yang

title: An Ensemble Learning Approach for Agricultural Greenhouse Mapping Based on Sentinel-2 Imagery: A Case Study of Weifang City
content: Agricultural greenhouses are an important component of protected agriculture, but their rapid and unregulated expansion may cause ecological and land-use problems. Accurate mapping of greenhouse distribution is therefore essential for sustainable agricultural management. This study proposes an ensemble learning approach for agricultural greenhouse classification using Sentinel-2 imagery in Weifang City, Shandong Province, China. Spectral bands and vegetation-related indices were extracted on the Google Earth Engine platform, and several machine learning classifiers were compared, including K-nearest neighbors, support vector machine, classification and regression tree, random forest, and gradient boosting decision tree. Their outputs were further integrated using a stacking ensemble strategy. The proposed ensemble model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.9821 and a Kappa coefficient of 0.9639, outperforming individual classifiers by approximately 5%–15%. Band ablation experiments showed that the ensemble model maintained high classification accuracy even with fewer input features, indicating its robustness and practical potential for medium-resolution greenhouse mapping. The results demonstrate that ensemble learning can effectively improve greenhouse identification from Sentinel-2 imagery and provide reliable support for regional facility-agriculture monitoring.
author: Xiaoqiang Yang, Xiaochuang Yao, Cong Ou, Jian Wang, Ying Guo, Quanlong Feng, Li Li, Bingbo Gao, Jianyu Yang

title: CAM-CD: Change-Aware Mamba for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Change detection (CD) methods based on Mamba and state-space models have attracted attention for their capacity to capture long-range spatial correlations with linear-time efficiency. However, most existing Mamba-based CD approaches use uniform scanning from generic vision backbones, which treats all spatial regions equally. This overlooks the sparsity and geometric diversity of real changes, resulting in diffused change responses. Driven by these limitations, we propose CAM-CD, a change-aware Mamba framework that approaches CD through sequential modeling. Unlike uniform scanning, CAM-CD aligns state-space modeling with sparse, structured changes by guiding state transitions toward change-relevant regions. Specifically, a change-aware adaptive scanning module utilizes spatial change priors to guide the scanning process, suppressing background noise with a small parameter increase. In addition, a selective scanning fusion module models bitemporal feature interaction as a path-dependent sequential processing mechanism, where recursive hidden states accumulate change-relevant information to gather discriminative evidence and enhance long-range contextual understanding. Comprehensive evaluations on four benchmark datasets show that CAM-CD consistently yields superior results compared to contemporary CNN-, transformer-, and Mamba-based methods. In particular, we achieve intersection over union gains of 1.09%, 0.68%, 2.28%, and 1.97% over the leading competitors on the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, SYSU-CD, and CLCD datasets.
author: Jinkun Xiong, Maofan Zhao, Xiaowen Wang, Gaofei Yin, Guoxiang Liu

title: Narrowband Suppressive Interference Suppression for UAV-Borne SAR Based on TSA-ISN
content: In complex electromagnetic environments, uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-borne synthetic aperture radar systems are highly susceptible to suppressive interference, which severely degrades imaging quality by obscuring target echoes. To address this challenge, we introduce an end-to-end deep network architecture termed temporal sequence adaptive interference suppression network (TSA-ISN). Considering the limited onboard computational resources of UAVs, this framework is engineered to operate directly on unprocessed intermediate frequency data in the time domain in order to preserve the crucial phase information, thereby obviating the necessity for auxiliary manual interventions and redundant calculations. To achieve adaptive feature extraction and interference suppression in a multidimensional domain, the TSA-ISN framework is equipped with the temporal attention module alongside the channel attention adaptive threshold module. In addition, a bidirectional temporal feature encoder module is employed to model global contextual information, thereby ensuring robustness against dynamic and bursty interference scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that TSA-ISN achieves strong interference suppression performance with relatively low model complexity and provides effective suppression against unexpected interference.
author: Wuqi Tian, Yue Yuan, Wenqian Xie, Jianchao Li, Xuanhe Liu, Linsheng Hou, Si Chen, Shuning Zhang

title: SAGINGeo: A Space–Aerial–Ground Integrated Framework for VGI Geolocalization in Multidisaster Scenarios
content: Volunteered geographic information (VGI) provides valuable geospatial cues for disaster management. However, existing geolocalization methods often overlook the potential of space–aerial–ground integrated views and rely on street view imagery (SVI) as the ground-level view, while underutilizing VGI that better reflects real-world conditions. In this article, we propose SAGINGeo, a cross-view geolocalization framework that improves VGI geolocalization by first integrating panoramic SVI and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery as intermediates to remote sensing imagery (RSI). Powered by a ViT-based unified multiview training scheme, SAGINGeo jointly models spatial information from space, aerial, and ground views to learn a shared representation. An anchor-guided reranking strategy is optionally applied to refine retrieval based on semantic similarity. To evaluate our framework, we constructed SAGINDisaster, the first multidisaster cross-view dataset integrating VGI, SVI, UAV, and RSI across four disaster types, comprising 2080 data groups, 118 560 images, and 2080 simulated UAV videos. Experiments show that SAGINGeo consistently outperforms the baselines with or without reranking assistance. With a single informative SVI and UAV image and an 8:2 data split, SAGINGeo increases Recall@1, Recall@5, Recall@10, and Recall@1% to 48.56%, 78.85%, 87.26%, and 76.20%, respectively. This study highlights the potential of combining multiview training to support disaster response and expand GeoAI applications. The code and dataset will be released upon acceptance.
author: Wenping Yin, Fabian Deuser, Jiancheng Jiang, Ziqi Liu, Xuanshu Luo, Zhedong Zheng, Martin Werner, Hao Li, Yong Xue

title: Characterizing Periodic Variations in Polar Ionospheric Total Electron Content and Their Correlation With Solar Activity
content: Understanding polar ionospheric dynamics and their coupling with solar activity is crucial for enhancing satellite navigation and high-frequency communication in extreme environments. This article investigates periodic variations in vertical total electron content (VTEC) derived via an undifferenced and uncombined precise point positioning method from 63 Antarctic and 99 Arctic global navigation satellite system stations (2013–2022), using Morlet wavelet analysis to examine cyclic characteristics and solar-activity correlations. Findings include: First, the quasi-27-day VTEC cycle was most prominent during high solar activity, with maximum relative amplitudes of 17.89% in the Antarctic and 8.90% in the Arctic. Annual cycle amplitudes were higher in the Antarctic (peak 4 TECU), whereas semiannual amplitudes were stronger in the Arctic (peak 2.0 TECU), likely reflecting thermospheric composition effects and asymmetric global circulation. Second, sunspot number correlated strongly with the quasi-27-day VTEC cycle. VTEC enhancements occurred either synchronously with solar activity or with a 1–2-day lag, and the Antarctic showed a faster response than the Arctic, possibly related to its more open geomagnetic configuration and enhanced susceptibility to solar-wind energy input. Third, in geomagnetic-coordinate-matched polar regions, the ∼36-day and semiannual spectral components showed different hemispheric prominence. The ∼36-day component appeared in both selected polar sectors, with hemisphere-dependent detectability and spectral prominence, while the semiannual component was generally more prominent in the Arctic but became more comparable in geomagnetic-coordinate-matched comparisons. The findings provide empirical constraints for high-latitude ionospheric modeling and polar space-weather applications.
author: Huajing Zhuo, Changzhi Zhai, Jian Kong, Yibin Yao, Chen Zhou, Ran Cui, Xueshuo Wang

title: Sea-Surface Current Vector Retrieval Using Squinted Multiaperture ATI-SAR (Sq-MA-ATI)
content: Ocean surface-current vector retrieval using conventional along-track interferometric synthetic aperture radar remains challenging because, under broadside viewing, the line-of-sight velocity has little along-track projection and a 2-D current vector cannot be determined from a single radial-velocity measurement. This article presents a squinted multiaperture along-track interferometry framework (Sq-MA-ATI) that introduces a physical azimuth squint and partitions two-channel echoes into multiple azimuth subapertures to generate several interferometric observations with distinct line-of-sight orientations over the same area. After focusing, each subaperture pair is processed interferometrically to estimate horizontal line-of-sight (HLOS) velocities, which are then assembled into an overdetermined linear system for the along-track and cross-track current components and solved by least squares to enable vector reconstruction and reduce random errors. Numerical error-propagation experiments, using parameterized HLOS noise and a common-resolution setting, further assess the effects of the number of looks, azimuth beamwidth, and physical squint angle. The approach is demonstrated in an airborne experiment over China’s Qiongzhou Strait under the squinted observation configuration. The beam-center HLOS velocity predicted from the retrieved vector agrees with the conventional along-track interferometry estimate about 1%. Compared with contemporaneous Global Navigation Satellite System drifter measurements, the retrieved current speed differs by 19.28% and the direction differs by 9.13$^\circ$. These results indicate that Sq-MA-ATI provides a practical route toward vector current retrieval from a single-pass squinted acquisition and may inform the design of future spaceborne along-track interferometric systems.
author: Ping Guo, Yongsheng Xu, Hanwei Sun, Weiya Kong, Lei Yang, Saichao Cao
